reviews.comment: Nice lady, great prof. She breaks down the concepts well. I recommend getting Chegg for this semester, because the homeworks can be very annoying if you are in a time crunch and need the work done. Pretty much all problems done in the class are on chegg so that is where you will get the real explanations.

Overall she is very nice but her grading is super strict. Large amount of homework every week plus quizzes plus projects and 3 exams so good luck. Her projects are poorly written and graded really strictly. Exams are very reasonable though and not graded that bad.

Tough class, but amazing professor. Her lectures were very well structured and she's an great teacher. 3  hard exams, two homework's a week, and a bunch of quizzes and in-class participation grades. She is also extremely kind to her students and wants to see them do well. Take her for this class!

What a wonderful professor! I genuinely enjoyed this class so much! She's so caring and genuinely wants her students to succeed, lots of homework but if you stay on top of it you will be fine. The concepts are super interesting and she sometimes does irl demonstrations too. You cant go wrong with McVay and will love this class, take her!

She's a pretty tough grader for exams, and the projects for the class are pretty harshly graded by the TAs as well. Also, the homework for the class is just generally terribly long and miserable. However, her lectures are pretty good and you get some free points for showing up and working. Also, the exams and quizzes are very doable.

MEEN 225 is a nightmare when it comes to homework, but Dr. McVay made the class pretty manageable. I would often spend 6+ hours a week per hw, but she taught well and was accessible. Easy grader on exams, but the TA grades the projects hard so make sure to do them perfect. Find a group to do the calculations together and format it pretty.

This class is so easy. If you took PHYS 206, you should be fine in this class as the first half of the class is pretty much just review. Every lecture either has a quiz or an in class assignment. In class assignments are easy and she usually gives you the answer. There is a homework for each lecture. Youll be fine if you do the homeworks.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy class if you are coming from something like physics 206, daily in class assignments can be annoying sometimes but they are all very easy and she gives answers.

Dr McVay is amazing. While there is a lot of homework every week, the homework's were always more challenging than what was on the quizzes or exams. The first two exams were not too bad as long as you studied a good amount, but the final, which isn't cumulative, was pretty tough. She gives a lot of partial credit on the exams though. Great lectures

First year teaching MEEN225 she has done it all. Those 50 minute lectures are very crammed with info and we submit a class activity at the end. The recitation doesnt take the whole time. Exams are 5 questions. Projects are the worst thing about the class. If you have a questions, she is happy to answer them to the best of her ability. She da goat.

Professor Mcvay is undoubtedly the best professor i've had. Her class is a difficult subject, if you do not go to class you will struggle in this course.However if you do go to class she does a great job of making it easy. I went from a C- in physics 206 to an A in meen 221. 
Exams are 5 questions each worth 20 points very generous with partialcred
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is the best Physics professor I ever had, she explains every detail of the topic and she answers questions clearly. exams are based on lectures so don't miss the class, work on the examples and do HomeWorks( about 8 questions per topic) then you should be fine!

Always answers questions from raised hands and stays after to talk to students. Alot of points were given free from in class participation work, which she also posts a video of online so everyone could get it even if the lecture was not attended. Homework could be tedious but not impossible.

The way McVay structures her lectures makes learning the material easy. There is pearson hw due for every class by the following class and in class work due every class besides quiz days. She lets you know when and what the quiz is over. Do the hw to study for the quizzes and study the review for the tests and you should be fine.
Best prof ever!!!! Made me like physics again

An outstanding professor with a straightforward and helpful lecture format: Introduce the topic and then work through examples. That's it. Just showing up to class gets you the best information and helps your grade with in-class work and quizzes. McVay and her TAs were also able to answer any question I had after class. Easy 5 stars.

Fair grader, material gets harder along the semester but she's really good at explaining so reach out (great in office hours), lots of Pearson HWs but they're great practice for exams. DO WELL ON THE QUIZZES, they're worth a decent amount of your grade and they're old exams questions!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mc-Vay does a great job breaking down statics into manageable chunks and explains things just well enough for me while still letting students think for themselves. She is very knowledgeable and she wants to see everyone succeed. She was my favorite prof this semester! Definitely take if possible.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: McVay is a great professor & teacher, and most of 221 is actually very easy conceptually.  What made this class annoying was the sheer amount of work she gave us.  Every week, without fail, there FIVE assignments.  Every week.  This class, by the end, became exhausting.  Again, very easy conceptually, but no curving, no mercy, lots of work.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, recorded lectures. Required in class work every lecture due at midnight, but you can watch the recording and do it if you're not there. Quizzes every week, common exams and homework.

Her lectures make so much sense, I highly recommend for statics, plus her lectures are recorded. Quizzes during class, but she lets you know when they are and what they are about- most of the points are graded over your solution, not the answer. Actually go over the reivews, it will immensely help your grade for the test. Highly recommend!

McVay is the goat for MEEN 260, she takes a terrible class into something manageable. Her exams were fair and her homework was tough but graded nicely. She also moved back lectures and labs so we could go see the eclipse. Her lecture notes were very helpful as well.

She's a solid teacher but this class just sucks. She's also kind of hard to hear if you're not near the front. However she is definitely one of the better 260 professors out there just because she's easy to understand and explains everything pretty well. She cancelled a lecture for the eclipse which was nice.
Dr. McVay was a great Prof, Tests are hard, but lots of homework helps with practice, Go to class, and don't be afraid to ask her questions, she gets that it's a hard class.

The homework assignments were unnecessarily hard and there's one every sunday. Her lectures are fine, but the material itself is pretty confusing and sometimes she couldn't explain things well. Her exams are fair, but they are graded tediously along with the homework. Make sure to show symbolic equations and don't make simple algebra mistakes.

Prof McVay was one of the best professors I had. MEEN 221 is inherently difficult but she makes things simple and breaks down the course into sections that help your understanding. Attend class and youll be on top of in class work. Homework piles up so keep up with that too. The exams are common and make sure to study and practice problems.

I really enjoyed Professor McVay's MEEN 260 course.  Her lectures did a solid job of explaining the fundamentals of each concept and the homework gave you great practice for the exams.  Her exams are not too difficult and if you practice the homework you should do well on them.  The lab can be time consuming but is not difficult overall.

Dr. McVay is great at explaining complex topics! Lectures are easy to follow. 2 homeworks a week which can sometimes be difficult. Provides exam review problems for each exam. Hosts a 2 hour exam review for each exam where you can ask questions. Overall very good instructor.
She is an amazing professor. Her lectures are very clear and easy to follow. While she does assign a lot of homework, it really does help you learn the material.

She is so passionate about statics and is really good at explaining concepts. Her tests are exactly like the homeworks and reviews. She does in class problems so you need to go to lectures. Homework is due two times a week but she only gives out 7-9 problems per homework so it doesn't take that long. Such a caring person, 10/10 reccommend.

Professor McVay is great!! She does tons of examples, accepts any questions, and care about you!! How you do in this class really matters on whether or not you do the homework and understand the material. If you miss lectures she usually posts them but make sure to watch them on the day they're done so you can get points for in class work.

Dr. McVay was an incredible professor. While I struggled in the class due to the amount of homework I can confidentley say that all of it was extremley neccessarey to understanding and succeding in the class, and if you have issues she helps you out alot during office hours. By far the best professor Ive taken here 100% reccomend

I absolutely loved Professor McVay. Her lectures were easy to understand and she tries to break down topics to make them as simple as possible. I would say the coursework is pretty normal. There are 2 homeworks due every week.  There are in class quizzes but they are fairly easy and they're always over content she covered in lecture.

Professor McVay is a great choice of professor for MEEN 221. The lectures are easy to follow and make a lot of sense, and she hosts review sessions for all her exams. The exams themselves are very fair and graded well. Overall a solid choice for this course.

Professor McVay is the best professor for this course. I took this course with a different professor the semester before and it seemed like rocket science, but with McVay, her teaching is easy to understand. She is a true example of how to teach. It is a lot of work but each work is detrimental to understanding the course and doing well.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic prof. Clear expectations, very caring and respectful, straightforward lectures, and publishes plenty of online material to help students learn. Take her for 221 if you can for sure.
Tries to have real demonstrations of the material whenever possible. Not a difficult class, but you do need to know all the material to pass.

Professor McVay is literally the sweetest woman and is very willing to help her students, but there's just something about this class that makes following along so hard. If you don't understand something figure it out sooner rather than later or you're going to get behind extremely fast. Jeff Hanson on youtube helped me a lot to fill in the gaps!!

MEEN 221 is a slightly difficult class but Dr. Mcvay is the best professor you could get. She teaches in a way that is easy to follow and her review sessions before exams are extremely helpful. She is also understanding and accommodating when it comes to missing quizzes. I would likely recommend her.

Dr. McVay is incredibly nice and makes a really tedious class very streamlined. The amount of homework she dishes out is overwhelming at first but it is very doable if you just get into a routine with it and keep up with the material. Her grading is very liberal as long as you show that you understand the concepts. Great prof!

Prof McVay is amazing! Best prof I took this semester. The class is not necessarily super difficult, but it is a lot of your. You have to stay on top of everything consistently if you want to do well. She does a great job however at making the workload manageable and understandable. Definitely take this prof if youve gotta get through this course.

Dr. McVay is an angel. She makes class enjoyable and lets you ask questions during lecture. Theres a ton of homework and this class moves super fast. So really this is like 2 classes of work. For the tests, study the hw and the ICW.

Dr. McVay was one of the best professors I've had. She was super caring and always cared to answer questions or reexplain a topic. The material was hard, but she explains it in a way that makes sense. Lots of homework, but it is for your benefit for exam preparation. Quizzes were pretty difficult. She is definitely the best choice for this course.

Her lectures cover the base knowledge and give easyish problems. She doesn't make the lecture problems difficult enough compared to HW and exams. HW, quizzes, and exams have the same level of rigor. There are opportunities to pad your grade in case you do poorly on an exam- reading quiz, HW, in-class work, quizzes. She's quite caring and accessible
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: MEEN 221 is a hard class, but Prof. McVay tries to make it as easy as possible. There is a lot of work in this class. Its usually two topics and two homework ever week. Try to do your homework without Chegg, that's the best way to prepare for the exams. There are in class work in every class so you have to go to class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall a very good prof, make sure to keep up with notes and examples, the quizzes and exams will follow their formatting. She's really good about answering questions and making sure students are following along. Make sure to set aside significant time for the homework for harder units.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McVay is awesome; however, since 260 is common across professors, it didn't make much of a difference. Took this class during COVID so it was all online. Worst class experience ever. They said 96% of students get As and Bs but I refuse to believe that since most people I know are getting Bs and Cs. Horrible class but McVay is a good bet.

It's the hardest class I have taken especially dynamics, in the end, kicks your ass. Recommended to take with a total of 12 hr coursework and dedicate most of your time on this course. She is the best if you have to take this class. I have attended other MEEN 221 reviews nothing comes close to how she teaches. DO not slack off and you will be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing. Pay attention & do the work (there is a lot) and you will understand the material & pass the class. She has set it up very well & is a wonderful, smart lecturer. Makes it easy to understand. Expect an increase in difficulty: examples > classwork > hw > quizzes > exam. Never a big leap if you dont miss a step
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. McVay was so kind and encouraging! Any time I visited her office hours, she was so helpful and really helped me feel I could excel in her class. It's not that hard of a class, and there are a lot of little assignments, meaning it's not the end of the world if you make a bad grade or two, or miss class once or twice. Best prof all semester!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Lots of homework, quizzes every class, her teaching is very good and clear unlike all the other profs I've heard of. Her exam reviews are better than the other profs as well. I attended different prof review and it was waste of time as couldn't follow it clearly. Exams are kinda hard even if you study but not impossible at all.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Two parts of the class. First half,McVay - stats. Second half Robbins - ECEN concepts. McVay taught the material well for the first half. However, she did not challenge us enough for the homework as the midterm was much harder. The part that sucks for the class is your grade is TA dependent (difference in grading) and all sections curved the same.

This professor is insanely hectic, she never curves, I received better grades on all tests than a friend taking another class, but he still received an A, while I got stuck with a B. She doesn't curve, most of those good ratings are written by her. She brought a question on the final that she herself wasn't able to answer during her office hours.
Tough grader. Her voice makes your brain explode.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My favorite professor yet! Tillie is caring and really knows her stuff. She gives a ton of partial credit and if you keep up with the material you should be fine!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor McVay is definitely the best professor I have ever had at Texas A&M University. MEEN 221 is a very hard and tough class, but she makes it very understandable. There are TONS of homework but it prepares you well for exams. To put in perspective, I got a C in Phys 218 but a B in MEEN 221 with McVay. Take her if you can 100%.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: McVay was a great professor for 221. Attendance is required since there are in-class quizzes and work. She is a great lecturer but I wish she would go into more detail with certain topics. She is a tough grader but does give a fair amount of partial credit. Overall, the homeworks though will be the key to your success on the exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. McVay is great choice. She conveys the class information clearly and neatly. Examples done in class are foundational; test questions are much harder. Theres a ton of work for only a small portion of your grade. Little room for error on tests if you're going for an A. Make sure to work lots of textbook examples to prepare for exams. Take her!
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. McVay is very clear in explaining concepts! She makes you do inclass work, but you can work on it with neighbors and it keeps you engaged. Everything is very fair in her classes. Her quizzes are a little random and if you keep up with the work, then you will do fine on them. She is definitely one of the better ones for 221 I would say.

McVay clearly explains the concepts covered and works plenty of examples to make sure students understand. She teaches using a flipped style and requires in class work, but allows you to work with classmates and answers student's questions helpfully. She makes attendance mandatory though, but she's definitely one of the better profs for the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is very respectable and is blunt about what you need to learn. She grades fairly and gives homework twice a week, in class work, reading quizzes, and pop quizzes. If you have a solid phys218 background it'll be easy for you.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: 75% grade from 3 exams, daily in class work for participation points, weekly in class quizzes, tedious but easy homework due twice a week. So class is mandatory. Felt babied in her class but she graded exams pretty nicely. Other profs have less HW and curve, she doesn't. If you have a strong background in PHYS218 though this class is a breeze

She is my favorite college professor that I've had. She is a tough grader and will take off points on your exam if you don't draw the FBD or write the original equation. However, you can make an A if you actually pay attention in class and don't miss assignments. The test questions are very similar to the HW questions, so be diligent when doing HW.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The lab portion of this class sucks, but the lecture and exams itself were so easy!!! Simple calculations and theoretical questions, very straightforward. McVay has powerpoint slides that you just read off of and takes notes on and that covers the homework. AWESOME!

If you take her get ready for a lot of work, you have homework due twice a week and daily work in every class. This may sound like a bad thing but it really helps to make sure that you stay on top of the material. She is very clear in class and provides a lot of chances to pratice in class.
There were daily in class work assignments. Weekly quizzes. On average 2 home works per week.
Mcvay is a great prof. Very clear lectures, very nice and helpful 1-on-1. 10/10, would recommend.

Dr. McVay is a great professor. She has very organized notes in class and posts them online the following week. Takes attendance through in class work, 1 every class, and online in class quizzes on fridays. The material is easy if you go to lecture and take good notes. She's great, I would definitely advise taking her!
The BEST 221 instructor. She's not a researching professor, so teaching is her number 1 priority. She explains well and gives great examples.
